manual.title: User manual
manual.intro: How the turnaround log is kept in Monstyk, screen by screen. The figures show the app in the language you have selected.

signIn.title: Signing in
signIn.body: Accounts are issued by the administrator, and each one is tied to a station: the app accepts operations only for the station on your account.
steps: Pick your language in the selector at the top of the sign-in page; the choice carries over into the app.
Sign in with the email address and password the administrator gave you.
A session lasts twelve hours — one shift. When it runs out, sign in again.
A deactivated account cannot sign in; the administrator has to reactivate it.

list.title: Your turnaround list
list.body: The list shows the turnarounds currently waiting on your station. A record appears when the previous station finishes its part and drops off once yours is done; a fully recorded turnaround that is still open stays with the last station on the route until it is closed.
steps: Narrow the list by date range, locomotive or status, or search by train or locomotive number, then press Filter; Reset clears every filter.
Open a turnaround by clicking the number in the first column or double-clicking its row.
Progress counts the operations already recorded; Elapsed is the time since the first one.
The list refreshes on its own — a turnaround handed over by another station shows up without reloading the page.

open.title: Opening a turnaround
open.body: Böyük Kəsik opens even train numbers, Tbilisi odd ones: the parity of the number carries the direction. Gardabani opens no turnarounds — it only receives them.
steps: Press New turnaround.
Type the train number. Böyük Kəsik opens even numbers, Tbilisi odd ones — the last digit decides.
The turnaround date defaults to today; change it when recording for a shift that started earlier.
Press Create. If the train is already on an unfinished turnaround, the app refuses and says so.

record.title: Recording operations
record.body: Operations follow a fixed sequence. You can enter only the next unrecorded step, and only on rows that belong to your station; everything else is shown read-only so you can see where the train is.
steps: Enter the operation's date and time in the Time field. It has to fall between the neighbouring operations — anything out of sequence is rejected.
Some steps ask for one extra value: a train number, a locomotive, a detachment reason, or the type and reason of technical work.
Press Save. The row gets a green tick and the name of whoever recorded it.
Clear removes a record, but only the most recent one — to correct an earlier step, clear the later ones first.
Show earlier operations expands the part of the route that is already behind the train.

close.title: Closing a turnaround
close.body: A turnaround can be closed once every required operation is recorded. Optional steps may stay empty; a conditional step is demanded only when the operation that triggers it took place.
steps: While required operations are missing, the header counts how many remain and no close button is shown.
When nothing is missing, press Close turnaround.
A closed turnaround becomes read-only; only an administrator can reopen it.

dashboard.title: Dashboard
dashboard.body: The dashboard summarises the period chosen in the date filter.
steps: Set From and To and press Filter; every counter, timing and downtime figure follows that range.
Time spent per station shows the average time each station holds the train, and the running time between stations.
Locomotive downtime shows how long each locomotive stood idle over the period.
Recent turnarounds links straight through to the records.

journal.title: Monthly journal
journal.body: The journal reproduces the sheet the staff has always kept: operations down the rows, turnarounds across the columns.
steps: Pick a month — and a single locomotive if you want — then press Filter.
Print outputs the paper form without the app's navigation.
Export to Excel writes the same grid to a file.
A dash means no record was made for that operation.

users.title: Users
users.body: Every account is created here. Operators belong to a station; administrators do not.
steps: Fill in the full name, email, role and password, then press Create user.
An operator must be assigned a station — the form will not save without one.
To change an existing user, edit the row and save; leave the password blank to keep the current one.
Accounts are deactivated, never deleted: a deactivated user cannot sign in but remains on every record they made.

fleet.title: Locomotives and reference lists
fleet.body: The registries behind the app's drop-downs live under Administration.
steps: Add a locomotive with its number, owner and depot.
Reference lists hold the technical work types, technical work reasons and detachment reasons offered on the turnaround form.
A record already used by a turnaround cannot be deleted. Deactivate it instead: it leaves the drop-downs while the history stays intact.

maintenance.title: Technical work
maintenance.body: Technical work takes a locomotive out of service; while the record stays open, that locomotive is not offered on any turnaround.
steps: Pick the locomotive, the type and reason of the work and the time it was sent off, then save.
When the locomotive comes back, press Mark returned — it becomes available again.
A record opened from a turnaround operation shows which turnaround it came from.

operations.title: Operation catalogue
operations.body: The operation sequence is data, not code: a change here reshapes every turnaround form at once.
steps: Each row declares its place in the sequence, its station, whether it is required, optional or conditional, and the extra fields it collects.
Parallel with marks a step that may be recorded alongside another rather than after it.
Edits take effect immediately; operations already recorded keep their values.
When a step should no longer be collected, disable it rather than delete it.

audit.title: Audit trail
audit.body: Every insert, change and deletion is written by the database itself, along with the user who made it — application code cannot bypass it.
steps: Filter by table, record or user to follow one object through its entire history.
Changes lists the fields that moved, with the values before and after.
Deleting an audit entry leaves no trace of its own — the confirmation warns you about exactly that.
